messages:
mira: quick postmortem from the prefetch granularity experiment — ran the granular-backoff policy on canary for 24h, here's what I observed.
alex: nice, TL;DR?
mira: ~12% median tail (p95) latency reduction on short-chat workloads, but memory high-water increased ~3-4% on GPU hosts.
chen: that memory increase matches my expectation: smaller prefetch chunks => more active allocations overlapping. did you see more eviction churn?
mira: slight uptick in swap activity for hosts with low buffer headroom. eviction count +18% during peak. however throughput improved and request queueing dropped.
leo: curious about the policy knobs. what exactly did you change?
mira: two new knobs in the warmup config: `prefetch.granularity_bytes` (default 2MB -> experimented with 512KB) and `prefetch.backoff_threshold` (fraction of buffer usage to trigger exponential backoff).
mira: config snippet: ```yaml
warmup:
  policy: granular-backoff
  prefetch:
    granularity_bytes: 524288
    backoff_threshold: 0.85
    max_concurrent_prefetches: 6
```
alex: how did this interact with safetensors vs mmap-backed checkpoints?
mira: because safetensors lets us address contiguous chunk reads, smaller granularity reduced initial stall for many short sequences. mmap files still benefited but had higher page fault overhead when chunk size was tiny.
chen: tradeoff sounds like a triangle: latency vs memory vs read overhead. any automatic tuning?
mira: we tried an adaptive controller that raises granularity when eviction rate > X and lowers it when p95 latency > Y. it converged but oscillated on mixed workloads. we added a gentle hysteresis and it stabilized.
leo: did you try layerwise prioritization instead of fixed chunking? i.e., prioritize embedding/first transformer layers on warmup queue first.
mira: yep, layer-priority helped for large models where early layers are hot. combination (layerwise + small prefix chunks) gave best p95 for chat-like prompts.
alex: what's the degradation mode? if we hit disk saturation does the policy back off to index-first warmup?
mira: yes, fallback path: on sustained disk I/O > 80% for > 30s, we switch to index-first + aggressive batching. infra-bot: canary rollout update: granular-backoff policy deployed to 6 hosts in us-west-2, currently serving ~1.2k req/s.
chen: any perf regressions in long-context batching workloads?
mira: long-context (8k+) saw negligible improvement, sometimes +2% latency due to extra KV cache churn. so we gate policy by workload profile.
leo: next steps?
mira: propose follow-up RFC to formalize policy interface: add `warmup.policy` pluggable strategy API, metrics for eviction-rate, prefetch-latency, and a small state machine for backoff. will draft today.
alex: please include the replay command and the perf traces (we'll need to reproduce on ci).
mira: replay command I used: `./tools/replay_warmup --trace=canary-2026-03-15.json --policy=granular-backoff --profile=short-chat`
chen: ping me on the RFC, want to add mmap heuristics and an option to prefer page-aligned reads.
leo: +1 to RFC. also add a canary checklist for memory HWM and eviction counts.
mira: noted. will link perf dashboards and raw traces in the RFC. thanks all :tada:
